text: The change report is one read on the decision base, GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/change-report, answered as a ChangeReportPage in which each RulePackageChangeEntry carries the legacy field list and a rulesChanged element of ruleId, added, changed and removed, and as text/csv with the same columns in the same order; the decisions of a version are counted in service on decision_log_entry by rule_version and rule_id over decided_at and are never taken from an aggregation operation of the decision-log API, whose filter set has no package version; the decision code of a governance entry and the checklist item-list code are values of LOV-DECISION and its sibling list; the per-service login is called the rwb-decision login (DP-02) because its name is not given.
why: The legacy story names the entry fields but not their nesting or the CSV order, and it attributes the per-version count to a decision-log read that filters by case, decision, rule, approver and date only, so neither the shape of the answer nor the operation behind the count can be taken from a source; without a stated reading the report cannot be built or tested, and the only owner of decision_log_entry is this service.

text: The split is made by table and not by the legacy module pointer: rwb-decision owns the change checklist on rule_package_version, the four approval checks and the change report, because it owns rule_package_version, rule_row and decision_log_entry under the R3 default ruling; rwb-case owns the case-side audit read and the impact count over open cases; rwb-access owns the screens, the roles and the permission matrix. The legacy module line 'P3 Case and workflow' and the P4 package recovery.accessadmin.rulepackages are kept as the legacy record and are not corrected in the legacy file.
why: The legacy story files the checklist and the report under P3 and P4 while the column and the tables it reads are P7's in the target, and the plan already splits the key across RWB-P3-E2041-APP, RWB-P4-E2041-APP, RWB-P7-E2041-APP and RWB-ITG-E2041-ITG; without the ruling two services would write the same column or the report would read a schema it does not own.

text: The legacy flag rwb.p3.rule-change-report is kept as the legacy reference and read as a parameter of rwb-decision through the parameters contract of rwb-case; it is not a code constant and it is not renamed in this run. Off: the change-report operation answers 404, the checklist part is ignored at load and the approve runs the registry checks only, so the version in force keeps serving. Feature flags of the target are a platform library concern, which this reading respects by holding no flag row in rwb_decision.
why: R3 default rulings put feature flags with the platform library and parameters with rwb-case, while the legacy flag carries a P3 prefix under the P7 owner of the registry; the flag decides whether the report exists at all, so a story cannot be built without a stated reading of who owns it and what off means.

impact: No business value changes. If the flag is renamed or moved to the platform library, one configuration row and the off-behaviour assertion of section 13 change; the criteria of section 7 do not.

text: LOV-DECISION, the package-version state list and the checklist item list are reference data read through the rwb-case reference-data contract with the version in force; the version states are LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK and REFUSED, the seven checklist items are the five caller members of the agreed schema of 16 November 2026 plus the five service-filled members read off the version row, and the decision code of a governance entry is a value of LOV-DECISION that is not written out in any source this story may read. No state, item or code is a constant of the code.
why: The legacy story writes the state LOADED and the decision log mapping as literals, and no list of decision codes or of the checklist item codes is carried by the extract, so a report cannot be validated or a state shown without a stated reading of where the values live and which values they are; Template and Rules R3 puts reference data with rwb-case and DP-07 is in the pattern table.

text: The report paging defaults and maxima and the checklist limits are parameters read through the parameters contract of rwb-case with the legacy values: page size default 50 and max 200, checklist part max 8 KB, changeRequestRef max 30, impactSummary max 1000, verifyNote max 1000 and rollbackPlan max 1000. A value above a maximum is refused with MSG-GEN-001 naming the member and its maximum, never clamped silently, and rules.testcases.min stays 50 where the registry reads it.
why: The legacy story writes the limits as numbers of its contract table and its exception path, and DP-06 requires every value a business person may change to be a parameter; a story cannot build the intake or the paging without a stated reading of which values are parameters and what a breach does.

text: This story tests the AC5 run and not the AC1 run of the legacy criterion set: ALLOCATION version ALLOC-2026.12 is loaded on 2026-12-08 with verify date 2026-12-08, approved on 2026-12-09 and valid from 2026-12-10, which is the only reading in which the verify item is on or after the load and before the approval.
